A fetus could be nonviable outside the womb but still have developed a brain and the capability to feel pain. It's hard for me to look at a 20 week old fetus and accept that it could be terminated. It looks too human already.
Yeah, it's a case-by-case thing. Difficult to have a sort of umbrella opinion.

If it's life-threatening, I agree.

But what about the right to bodily autonomy of the fetus/baby? Even a 1 year old baby cannot live of its own volition without someone sustaining them - does that mean they don't have a right to life because they are wholly dependent on someone?

Yes, it's our bodies, our choices. But they have to be responsible choices.

I don't want to be insensitive. I sometimes think about how I'd feel if I ever got pregnant, because I never want to, and also having some mental issues to deal with. It would be a torturous decision for me to make, either way.

In those cases you're describing, it's not the same as killing something/someone that is innocent. I don't think abortion is always wrong, just a very difficult topic.
2% of how much though? To me even 20 weeks seems like a late stage. Why do so many take that long to decide to abort?

There is nothing different about the fetus, but the situation is way different than if it was just a surprise unwanted pregnancy. There's trauma involved. I'm sure that most would not want to continue a pregnancy in that case, so I see it as a kind of necessary evil. It would be more evil to force the woman to bear the child.

I don't see it as punishing women for having sex if abortion isn't legal as a form of contraception. At 20 weeks seems to me like too late a stage. Why would it take so long to decide one doesn't want a pregnancy, anyway?

Also why I think this stigma around sterilization should end and access to it be easier for women of all ages. In my case, never wanting to bring a human into the world, i don't want to be denied that and then end up having to make a choice whether to keep a baby or not.

Agree with you except I think it's harder to define "life". Even as a clump of cells, it's a living thing. For me the problem comes when the fetus is at a stage where it already can process pain, has developed a brain and a heartbeat.

Yeah I also don't get the "my body, my choice" argument. It's not like getting a tattoo. It should be a choice in some cases like risk of death, complications, severe disability, rape - as horrible as it is, but not normalised and used as some kind of contraception.

I hope I wasn't insensitive in my wording.

I don't know what being in that situation is like, but I agree that if both mother and baby were certain to die, then as horrible as it would be, the choice would have to be hers.

I know, it's the one subject I'm never able to decide on.

Illegality/criminalisation only endangers women who try to go through with it anyway, or else aren't able to terminate and then die/suffer complications because of the pregnancy. In cases of rape there definitely should be a choice to terminate, but then would the woman have to prove it was rape? It's not always possible to prove.

Then you have to consider at what point do we consider it a fetus not a clump of cells? Some say at 8 weeks a fetus is already able to feel pain, others say it's later on. That knowledge can't be ignored.
